name: Sefe
subtitle: the planet with no mirrors
story: On Sefe nothing shines: not water, not glass, not eyes. So nobody sees their own face, and other people have to tell you what it looks like. Lovers trade descriptions on the first night, mothers go first, and barbers finish every haircut with a long, careful one. Oskar's wife died in the winter. He still comes in every month, and the barber doesn't say a word.
hook: A planet for people who keep every nice thing anyone's said about them.
cover: Nobody here knows what they look like.

episode.opener:
On Sefe, nobody knows
what they look like.

beats.note: a sunless fog: no stars, no moon, nothing to catch the light

beats.text:
Other people
have to tell you.

Lovers trade descriptions
on the first night.

'A face like bread,
when it's done.'

Mothers go first.
Every man on Sefe
thinks he's handsome.

Barbers end each haircut
with a long, careful description.

Oskar's wife died in the winter.
He still comes in every month.

episode.end: He stays the way she said.
episode.caption:
Two men outside a barber's, saying nothing.

Sefe: 8,000 people, a 30-hour day, no moons, and not one shiny thing. Water is matte, glass is frosted, and eyes don't catch the light, so you never see your own face. You know it the way you know the weather somewhere else: from what people tell you. Parents describe a new baby to itself every night. Portrait painters mainly listen. A good description is the most romantic thing you can give anyone here, and people keep theirs for life.

I asked a stranger what I looked like. She said 'lost'.

(On Earth, still water sends back only about 2% of the light that falls straight onto it. It was enough for Narcissus.)

Where do you keep the nicest thing anyone's said about you?

first_comment: Oskar's barber: Every month. Not a word. He tips double.

short.kicker: A planet for people who keep every compliment.
